section.title: Latest News
section.p:
Latest news of the
pmMDA
for the community.

ul.li: Trunk has moved to 0.3.x. The first official release of this trunk is scheduled for June 2005. The goal is to deliver the new version shortly after the project is one year old.

section.title: pmMDA 0.3.x
section.p: Current development trunk and not released. Effort is put in enhancing the documentation, the usability and smoothing rough edges.

ul.li: The development environment was updated to Eclipse 3.1.1 and Open Office 2.0. The JDK was upgraded to the latest available version JDK-1.5-06.

Effort was put in the serie to use only actual versions of external components and document all dependencies. The web site was updated to better support forrest capabilities. The documents were updated to use the capabilities of forrest 0.6. Upon release of version 0.7 the web site documentation was migrated to forrest 0.7.

The application can be run with JDK 1.5. The source code will be ported to use the new features of the language. Refactoring will be applied to support loop for iteration, enumeration types and generics. The JavaDoc quality will be increased.
The copyright notices are updated to reflect modifications performed during 2005.

section.title: pmMDA 0.2.x
section.p: These releases are used in technical university projects supported with grants of the Swiss transfer projects sponsored from the Swiss governement.

This releases serie is the first step from a working prototype used in a handful projects to an application which can be used by developers to generate the business model of their applications. The major innovations are.

ul.li: The major goal of the latest version of the series is to remove identify errors and have a stable code base. Refactoring was applied to clean major public interfaces.
The release candidate 2 was promoted to official candidate 0.2.9 without changes.

The development team has released pmMDA 0.2.9-RC-2 release. The candidate date is 30 October 2004. This release should be run with JDK.1.5.0-RC. The test applications created with the provided ArgoUML model can be build with the provided ant tasks and run with the available scripts located in scripts/tests. All open issues of the 0.2.x line are corrected.
A major contribution to pmMDA users is the introduction of a validation framework detecting errors in the settings of tagged values and stereotypes in the model.

An initial version of a complete example is provided with a tutorial. The provided ant files compile and run the tutorial in all supported modes: as 2-tiers application, as CORBA client/server and as J2EE client/server. The J2EE mode requires a JBoss installation. The database is the lightweight solution HSQL and does not require additional installation. To compile the tutorial JDK 1.4 or higher and Ant 1.5 or higher are required.
The documentation and project web site is generated with forrest version 0.6. A script loads the new web site on sourceforge if desired.

pmMDA is now available on Sourceforge under
pmMDA
. The published version should run without configuration on any workstation where Java JDK 1.4 or higher and Ant 1.6 or higher are available.

pmMDA can be run as a seperate application delivered as a set of jar files and a startup scripts. A pmMDA properties file is provided. The user can modify it to reflect its project structure. The property file support variable declarations as in Ant build files.
The velocity templates are delivered in a seperate directory. Architects can tailored them to their application needs and coding guidelines.

A set of cartridges are provided. The cartridges provide support for 2-tiers applications, CORBA based client/server, and J2EE based client/server applications. Support for the OJB persistence mechanism is provided.
Cartridges are pluggable in the application. Power users can write their own cartridges to implement business model code generation specific to their own frameworks.
A complete example is provided to ease the learning how to use pmMDA tool.
The iterator pattern described in Bloch's book is now used in the source code and code genertor templates. The JavaDoc documentation is now available for almost all items.

section.title: pmMDA 0.1.x
section.p: This releases serie ported the old code generation tool to the Java environment. These releases are not more supported.

ul.li: Support for CORBA based client/server application and OJB is provided.
